title: A Graphical Criterion for Front-Door Formula Validity with a Singleton Mediator in ADMGs
banked_reason: The delivered singleton-gateway iff is mathematically sound, but the score gate caps it at subfield (7.3 < 7.4) because multi-gateway completeness, a general small-model theorem, and arbitrary witness lifting remain open.
gap_reasons: It does not solve the advertised complete verifier for multi-vertex gateway sets, the general small-model property, or arbitrary projected-model lifting, all of which remain explicit open questions.

Rejection establishes formula invalidity but does not provide the promised per-instance fixing-functional-or-hedge diagnosis of target identification; the note proves only the logical distinction and a representative example.
These scope limits, together with the absence of a practical implementation or broader worked applications, keep the package below flagship significance despite clearing the field floor.

[D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.3 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted a graph-only verifier for the standard front-door functional and proved an exact, cardinality-uniform iff theorem for singleton gateways in arbitrary finite selection-free ADMGs, including positive rational countermodels and motif-specific witness lifting. Both final mathematical panels passed without findings and all cited dependencies were source-attested. The field target failed only at the score ceiling: arbitrary multi-gateway completeness, a general small-model theorem, general reverse projection lifting, and per-instance fixing-or-hedge diagnostics remain separate open programs.
tldr: We prove the exact cardinality-uniform graph-only criterion for every finite ADMG with a singleton gateway: \(FDValid(G,T,Y,\{Z_0\})\) holds if and only if \(C_3(\operatorname{lp}_{\{T,Z_0,Y\}}(G),T,Y,Z_0)\) holds. Acceptance has a checkable equality derivation, and rejection has a strictly positive finite rational witness obtained by routing one of seventeen three-node obstruction motifs through the original graph and adding full-support noise. The lift is motif-specific, not surjectivity for arbitrary projected SCMs; multiple gateways and the complete all-ADMG verifier remain open.
gap: The strongest direct graphical result gives a sufficient region and a necessary obstruction region but leaves a residual class undecided. General identification algorithms answer whether some formula exists, not whether this supplied formula is correct, and current practical verification guarantees are relative to chosen parametric families.
fill: Develop a terminating normalization that combines graph-certified probability reductions with nested fixing identities, prove completeness by reducing every irreducible negative branch to a realizable obstruction, and audit the proof against exact three- and four-node calculations and binary-versus-ternary identities.
